question: What is the primary objective of medical asepsis in clinical practice?

options.A: Reducing the number and spread of microorganisms
options.B: Preventing airborne transmission of viral spores
options.C: Sterilizing surgical instruments prior to use
options.D: Eliminating all microbial life from an object

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on decreasing pathogen load and limiting transmission, unlike surgical asepsis which seeks complete sterility. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why must hand hygiene still be performed immediately before donning medical gloves?

options.A: Soap permanently alters the pH of the epidermal outer layer
options.B: Moist skin inside gloves accelerates rapid microbial proliferation
options.C: Glove manufacturing leaves toxic chemical residues on surfaces
options.D: Synthetic polymers chemically react with residual body oils

explanation: The warm, enclosed space inside a glove creates an ideal breeding ground for bacteria already present on the skin if hands are unwashed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which clinical scenario strictly requires the use of clean medical gloves?

options.A: Assisting an ambulatory patient to walk down the hallway
options.B: Measuring a patient's blood pressure over an intact shirt sleeve
options.C: Feeding an independent adult patient a standard hospital meal
options.D: Emptying a urinary drainage collection bag in the ward

explanation: Urine is a bodily fluid with high potential for contamination, requiring barrier protection during disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What dual purpose do medical gloves serve in the hospital environment?

options.A: Enhancing manual grip strength when handling wet clinical equipment
options.B: Providing complete hand sterilization during prolonged surgical procedures
options.C: Protecting staff from infection and preventing pathogen transfer to patients
options.D: Replacing the need for routine hand washing between patient rooms

explanation: Gloves act as a two-way shield, safeguarding both the healthcare worker and the patient from cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is a key physical design difference between examination and surgical gloves?

options.A: Surgical gloves are packaged in non-sterile bulk cardboard dispensers
options.B: Examination gloves feature exact sizing numbers for each finger length
options.C: Surgical gloves are manufactured with specific left and right hand shapes
options.D: Examination gloves include extended cuffs to cover surgical gowns

explanation: Surgical gloves are anatomically shaped for left and right hands to reduce fatigue and improve dexterity during long procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: When is it appropriate to utilize non-sterile examination gloves in patient care?

options.A: During an open reduction and internal fixation of a fractured femur
options.B: While inserting a central venous catheter into the subclavian vein
options.C: When performing a routine venipuncture on intact skin
options.D: During the surgical repair of an open abdominal hernia

explanation: Routine tasks like venipuncture involve contact with blood but do not breach sterile body cavities, making clean examination gloves sufficient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which glove material provides the greatest resistance to punctures and chemical exposure?
explanation: Nitrile synthetic rubber offers superior puncture resistance and durability against harsh chemical agents compared to vinyl or latex. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: A staff member develops contact urticaria and respiratory symptoms when handling certain medical supplies. Which glove material is the most likely cause of this reaction?
explanation: Natural rubber latex contains proteins that frequently induce Type I immediate hypersensitivity reactions, presenting as hives or respiratory distress. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: What part of a sterile glove is touched first when donning them using the open method?

options.A: The inside of the cuff fold
options.D: The outer edge of the wrapper

explanation: Touching only the inside of the cuff fold protects the exterior sterile surface of the glove from contamination by unwashed or unsterile hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: During sterile glove application, what is the proper technique for putting the second glove onto the non-dominant hand?

options.A: Use your teeth to adjust the wrist placement after both hands are inside
options.B: Slide the sterile gloved fingers underneath the outer cuff fold of the second glove
options.C: Ask an assistant to hold the open cuff while you insert your hand quickly
options.D: Grip the outside finger surface with your bare hand and pull firmly upward

explanation: Gloved-to-gloved contact using the cuff fold maintains sterility by ensuring skin never touches the outer surface of the second glove. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: Where should used contaminated gloves be disposed of immediately after removal?

options.A: In the patient's bedside trash can
options.B: In your uniform pocket for later disposal
options.C: On top of the medication preparation cart
options.D: Inside a designated clinical waste bin

explanation: Contaminated barriers must go directly into biohazard or clinical waste receptacles to prevent accidental exposure in the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the primary rationale for turning gloves inside out as they are removed?

options.A: To trap potential pathogens on the inner surface away from skin
options.B: To compact the volume of waste inside the disposal bin
options.C: To prevent the latex material from sticking to your fingers
options.D: To make it easier for housekeeping staff to sort hospital trash

explanation: Inverting the gloves encapsulates the contaminated exterior surfaces, preventing infectious material from contacting the nurse's skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT acceptable when managing disposable medical gloves?

options.A: Applying alcohol-based hand rub to soiled gloves for reuse
options.B: Performing hand hygiene immediately after removing soiled gloves
options.C: Selecting a nitrile glove size that fits the hand snugly
options.D: Changing gloves between different body sites on the same patient

explanation: Disposable gloves are single-use items; chemical disinfectants degrade their structural integrity and they cannot be safely reused. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: A nurse wearing gloves touches a patient's infected pressure ulcer and then immediately touches the computer keyboard at the nurses' station. What has occurred?

options.A: The creation of a fomite-mediated cross-contamination route
options.C: An effective sterilization of the computer equipment
options.D: A standard violation of surgical asepsis guidelines only

explanation: Wearing contaminated gloves outside the immediate care zone transfers pathogens to high-touch environmental surfaces, endangering others. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: Under Standard Precautions, when must healthcare personnel wear gloves?

options.A: Whenever anticipated contact involves blood, body fluids, or non-intact skin
options.B: Throughout the entire duration of an eight-hour hospital shift
options.C: Only when caring for patients with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV
options.D: Exclusively during sterile surgical procedures performed in the theatre

explanation: Standard Precautions mandate barrier use for any potential exposure to blood, body fluids, secretions, excretions, and non-intact skin for all patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)

question: A patient is admitted to the ward with a confirmed multidrug-resistant organism spread via touch. Which transmission-based precaution category applies, requiring mandatory glove use upon room entry?
explanation: Contact Precautions are designed to prevent the spread of infectious agents transmitted by direct or indirect contact with the patient or their environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)
